To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 15N and/or 13C stable isotopes of MDMA samples can be used to discriminate the synthetic origin of the samples, that the 15C isotope ratio is a more reliable indicator of the synthetic origin of MDMA than the 15N isotope ratio, and that both the delta13C and delta15N values can be used to distinguish between different synthetic routes to MDMA.
the 15N contents and 13C contents of synthetic MDMA are not correlated with one another, and that the 15 N contents of MDMA are not correlated to the origin of the N-atom in the MDMA molecule.

1. the delta15N value of MDMA is not a reliable indicator of the synthetic route by which it was manufactured; 2. delta15N values are influenced by the origin of the N-source, the route by means of which it was converted to MDMA and the conditions of reaction; and 3. the delta15C values of MDMA are not a reliable indicator as to the origin of its N-source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of stable isotope analysis as a means of identifying the source of MDMA and the synthetic routes used to manufacture it.
a number of aspects of the synthesis of MDMA.
the development of a method to discriminate between MDMA samples derived from different routes of synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 13C and, to a lesser extent, 15N contents in MDMA samples can provide information on the synthetic route and the origin of the precursors.
the 15N and/or 13C isotope ratio of a sample of MDMA is not a reliable indicator of the synthetic route by which that sample of MDMA was prepared.
the delta15 N values of MDMA samples are strongly dependent upon the delta15N value of the source of N used in the synthetic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 15N contents and 15N-13C correlations of MDMA can be used to provide information about the synthetic origin of MDMA but that this approach cannot be applied to the discrimination between the synthetic origins of different samples of MDMA.
the delta15Ns of the N-atom of MDMA samples synthesised by different routes from different N-sources can be correlated to the delta15Ns and the origins of the N-sources.

the delta13C values for synthetic MDMA can be used to identify the origin of the aromatic moiety, but not to distinguish between different synthesis routes, whereas the delta15N value can be used to discriminate between different routes but not to distinguish the source of nitrogen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the delta15NMMA values of MDMA samples can be used as an indicator of the synthetic origin of the sample.
it is possible to identify the synthetic route by which a given MDMA sample has been made, but only by the use of a suite of isotope ratio measurements.
the delta15 N values of synthetic MDMA are not useful in the forensic context for determining the synthetic origin of MDMA samples.
